title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for multi-tool & parallel calls with injected results and retry semantics
author: Asha Patel
body:
Context and motivation: customers and internal evals show growing usage patterns where a single inference can request multiple tool calls (e.g. data fetch + enrichment + external action). We also see more applications issuing parallel tool calls to improve latency and cover fan-out workflows. Current execution semantics made it awkward to: (1) inject multiple tool results back into the model in a deterministic way; (2) run tool calls in parallel while preserving ordered result injection for tokens/structured outputs; and (3) safely retry failed tool calls without causing duplicated side effects. This PR introduces a set of runtime and API ergonomics improvements to address those gaps.

Summary of changes: 
- New execution orchestration for multi-tool calls that supports parallel dispatch with deterministic result injection ordering by user-provided "injection_point" metadata. This lets callers run tools in parallel but control where each tool's output is inserted into the model context.
- Idempotent retry policy framework for tool execution: tools can opt into an idempotency token in the tool call payload; the runtime performs best-effort deduplication and provides explicit retry metadata to the caller for non-idempotent tools. Backoff and max-attempts are configurable per-route.
- Streaming compatibility: streaming responses in OpenAI-compat mode now include tool_call events and tool_result injections as separate event types to avoid truncation or interleaving with partial token events. We added a small state machine to the streaming mux to ensure tool_result chunks are emitted atomically.
- Structured output support: updated structured_output enforcement so tool-result injection can be validated against the declared output schema before injection into the model context; validation failures are surfaced as structured errors to the client.
- API: extended the OpenAI-compat tool call schema to include `injection_point` (string), `idempotency_token` (string, optional), and `retry_policy` (object encoded as string for compat). The new fields are backwards-compatible: old calls still work.
- Telemetry and observability: added metrics for parallel_tool_calls, tool_injection_latency, retry_attempts, and tool_dedup_hits. Added per-tool traces that span client->runtime->tool-executor for root-cause analysis.
- Tests & docs: added unit and integration tests and a migration guide in docs/tool-calling.md with examples.

Design notes: 
- Ordered injection: callers can provide an `injection_point` tag like `before_step_2` or `after_step_n`. If omitted, the runtime injects tool results in the order tools were declared in the call. When executing tools in parallel, the runtime buffers results and injects them atomically according to the resolved ordering.
- Retries and side effects: the runtime attempts deduplication by tracking idempotency_token for a TTL per-route. For non-idempotent tools we surface `retryable: false` in the tool invocation response; callers should handle compensation externally.
- Streaming & OpenAI compat: to preserve streaming stability for clients that parse token streams, we emit `event: tool_call_start`, `event: tool_call_end`, and `event: tool_result_injected` frames. Clients that don't understand these frames will still receive a final `response` frame with the aggregated content.

Migration and rollout: 
- This change is non-breaking for existing callers. Consumers who want deterministic injection ordering or safe retries should opt into the new fields.
- We are shipping this behind a feature flag `tool_exec_ergonomics_v2` and will enable for 20% of traffic initially.

Checklist: 
- [x] Runtime orchestration implementation
- [x] OpenAI-compat schema extension and streaming frames
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Performance microbenchmarks and canary run
- [x] Migration docs and samples

Related: ENG-1254 (multi-tool orchestration), ENG-1299 (retry framework), SUP-4021 (customer request), design doc: /docs/design/tool-calling-exec-ergonomics-v2.md

Release notes: see `release_notes` field.

Why this matters: improves latency for multi-tool flows (by enabling parallel dispatch), reduces developer friction for injecting results, and makes retries safer for production integrations.

review_comments: Diego Morales: Please expand on how we ensure deduplication across runtime restarts — is the idempotency_token persisted?

Asha Patel: We persist token -> result mapping in the per-route KV for ttl=24h. If the runtime is recovered, the mapping is rehydrated from the primary store. See src/runtime/tool_executor.py:dedup_index implementation.
Satomi Yamada: There was an e2e flake in streaming tests where partial token frames were interleaving with tool_result frames. Can you make the buffer drain atomic?
Asha Patel: Fixed in c3e1b71 and added a mux state machine in src/api/streaming_mux.py; re-ran e2e and it passes consistently.
Noah Singh: What are the perf implications for small batch sizes? We should include a benchmark and a knob to disable parallelism per-route.

Asha Patel: Benchmarks included — median latency for 1-tool single-call is unchanged; worst-case +~3% median latency for extremely small sequences due to buffering. Added config `parallel_execution_enabled` per-route to opt out.
Diego Morales: Approved pending documentation addition about non-idempotent tool guidance.
Satomi Yamada: Approved after adding structured error examples to docs.
Release Manager (automated): Changelog entry added to release-notes/next.md
ci_checks: e2e streaming: initial flake -> rerun -> pass
perf benchmarks: added microbench, perf regression <=3% for small-batch worst-case
release_notes:
- tool-calling: parallel dispatch with ordered injection_point support
- tool-calling: idempotency token + retry policy for safer retries
- streaming: new tool_call/tool_result_injected event frames (OpenAI-compat)
- observability: metrics and traces for parallel tool calls and retries
Migration: opt-in via `tool_exec_ergonomics_v2` feature flag. See docs/tool-calling.md for examples and guidance on idempotent tooling.
